title: Uniqueness of weak solutions for the power-law Navier-Stokes-Voigt problem
author: Ankit Kumar, Hermenegildo Borges de Oliveira and Manil T. Mohan
work: Optimal existence of weak solutions for the power-law Navier-Stokes-Voigt equations
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 3.4 of the article (source label UniT, source0.tex lines 770--772), the uniqueness theorem of the paper: under the assumptions of the two existence theorems, for $p>1$ when $2\leq d\leq 4$ and for $p\geq d/2$ when $d>4$, the weak solution of the power-law Navier-Stokes-Voigt problem is unique in the class of weak solutions of Definition 3.1. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 129-line proof at source0.tex lines 2499--2627. H2: the proof is a genuine energy-method comparison of two weak solutions with a non-Newtonian stress tensor rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must subtract the two solutions and exploit the monotonicity of the $p$-Laplacian-type operator, handle the Voigt regularisation term through the difference of the symmetric gradients, control the convective term with the help of the Gagliardo--Nirenberg and Sobolev embeddings in the ranges of $p$ and $d$ stated in the theorem, and close the Gronwall argument in the correct weighted norm. Reproducing that monotonicity-and-embedding argument for the full range of exponents is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
